paragraphs: Rabbi Yannai, father-in-law of Rabbi Ami.
Mentioned in Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:11, saying: “Everyone agrees that Solomon composed Kohelet last.”[^1][^2]

notes.text: חמוהי explicitly means father-in-law, not brother-in-law. The exact Midrash Rabbah -- TE opening passage at Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:1, text index 9, explicitly gives Rabbi Yannai, father-in-law of Rabbi Ami, and the statement that all agree Kohelet was said last. Its surrounding discussion concerns Solomon’s books, supporting Solomon as the understood subject, rather than Kohelet itself speaking.

The supplied שהש״ר פ״א־יא is retained as Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:11. The matching passage is in the retrieved 1:1 opening segment; a separate 1:11 response is archived. The correspondence between Hyman’s locator scheme and this digital scheme is not adjudicated, and the source is unchanged. The exact matching qualifier/passage supports both full Rabbi expansions, without identity admission.
